BIRMINGHAM, June 20, 1857.
The indoor and outdoor harangues which have
been lately delivered in this city by man named
Murphy who styles himself the "Ant- -Remanist
Lecturer" and who in all his disoourses inveighs
vehemently against Popery and the ceremonies,
rites and sacraments-particularly the COMES
sional-of the Catholic Church, induced very
great disturbances here during the last few days.
Very intense excitement prevails among the
people, and at one time last Tuesday the aspect
Of affairs was exceedingly serious.


At least one hundred thousand people were
turned out in the streets and an snraged mob had
possession Of the city for some time.


They sacked several houses.


The rioters marched through the streets singing
"Glory. glory, hallelujah," "John Browns cho-
rus" and other airs Of this class.


The authorities were active in defence Of order.
The Riot act was read by the magistrates.


Troops were hurried to the city from Manches-
tor and placed in position in the streets. Tho
military did not fire, however.


The city police were out in full force, the men
using their cutlasses.


Several of the rioters were wounded but none,
as yet reported, killed.


The excitement is now somewhat lulled, and 1t
is expected tho active disturbances are ended.
Murphy, who is under the protection Of the
protestant Electoral Union," has persisted in
his course. and every night delivers offensive Ian
guags at much length sgainst the Roman Catholic
church, ridiculing its rites. &c.


Attempts have been made to renew the distur-
bance out Of doors, but they have been put down.
The city 10 comparatively quiet At present.

When autumn days come, Nature, like a
retired merchant, changes its manner from
thrift and bustling industry to langqid lei
sure and to oStentatlOus luxury SE4,fle sun
rises later and sets earlier than when it
had all the summers crops on hand, and


was playing universal husbandman. There
IS no nest building now, and no bird sing
1ng-which is purely domestic arrange
ment, designed, on the birds part, to keep


peace in the family while the children are


being raised, and laid aside as soon as the
young birds are off their hands. Mornings
come fieeced in mists, which hang over
streams and low, moist places. The sun
plays with them, but they perish in chis
arms. A few belated flowers yet keep
watch, but chiefly the asters. which fringe
the fields, star the edges of forests, and like
a late conner at feast, seem bent upon
making up for the lost time. At
nights, crickets and katy dds scrape
their shrill viols and fill the air with
stridulous music. Over all the shrinking
fields, the trees lift up their gorgeous foli-
age, and, like those who wait for the mar
riage bell and the bridegroom, they shine
out in glorious apparel. The hills, forest
clad. are become the Lords young sons,
and, like Joseph, they are dressed in coat
OF many colors. October days, short be-
tween horizons, reach higher into the vault
than any days of the year, and through
them che seasons seem to look with soften
ed sadness, as one who, in the calm of age,
meditates on all the mistakes of his past
life, and solemnly thinks upon the advanc-
ing future. Along the fence rows, where
seeds and late berries may be found, birds
hop silently, as If ashamed to be SEEM
Soon they will change their solitary ways
and collect in hocks. To-day, the fields
will swarm with them; tomorrow, there
will not be one left. and they will be pick
ing their food many degrees of latitude
south. ..rf - III . -r -f

BY MATTHEW ARNOLD.
Creep into thy narrow bed,
Creep, and let no more be said
Vain thy onset all stands fast;
Thou thyself must break at last.
Let the long contention cease
Geese are swans, and swans are geese.
Let them have it how they will
Thou art tired; best be still
They out-talked thee, Kissed thee, tore thee.
Better men Jared thus before thee:
Fired their ringing shot and passed,
Holly charged-and broke at last.
Charge once more, then, and be dumb
Let the victors, when they come,
When the forts of folly fall,
Find thy body by the wall.

ST, LOUIS, July 10.-An Omaha dispatch
says: On Saturday morning some soldiers
from Fort Laramie went to Rafferty's
rancho, five miles distant, and demanded
whisky, anl because they were refused,
threatened to burn the rancho. A second
demand being refused, the soldiers attacked
the store of Keeper and one of their num-
ber was shot. The soldiers then formed
line and fired several shots at the ranche.-

fifty soldiers, arrested the occupants of the
rancho, and took the safe and desks in the
building. The safe was afterwards robbed
and the rancho burned by the soldiers. The
proprietor estimates his loss at sixty thou
sand dollars. A court martial at Fort Lar
annie was examining the matter.

The MOravian Seminary at Bethlehem Pa,
has long been widely popular as high school
for young ladies. It's trustees and principal
are probably as competent and faithful as
those of almost any similar academy Yet it
seems that they have but one bedroom, 25 by
10 feet, for their eight servant-girls, and that
this room, on the basement floor adjoining the
Kitchen had but single window and q door |;
and that these being closed Gas OF course they
usually were while the girls slept, there was
absolutely no ventilation, and no admission OF
fresh air True there was single tiue,
which led from this room up into the pupils
dning-roOm overhead but this ffue was gen
orally shut up, or only opened through
stoye-pipe which led into the chimney. The
stove being taken down on the return of
Spring, the pipe was allowed to remain and
down this pipe the gas from the stove above
was regularly driven, filling the girls bedroom
with its poisonous fumes, until, on Sunday
night last, it killed two of them outright, and
probably will kill one more. OF the remainder,
two were badly and two more but slightly in
jured The eighth did not retire till toward
morning, when she discovered the mischief,
though she did not comprehend it till daylight.


Of course, this is not murder, but ignorance
gross, shameful, guilty ignorance. No person
has any right to undertake the most respOn-
sible charge of a seminary who does not know
that close bedroom is perilous to the health
and life of even one human being, and more
than eight times as perious when its inmates
are increased to eight. Had the managers of
the Mor9yian Seminary known what i. yas
their duty to know, and had they nevertheless
packed these eight girls into one unventilated
room, they ,rould have been murderers of the
darkest dye. Their ignorance palliates, but does
not excuse, their wrong-doing. What will pal
late the crime of the next set of, wholesale
homicides by means of unventilated bedrooms,
or class-rooms or halls for public meetings.

sitting in the Circuit Court this morning, rem
dered his decision in a habeas corpus case on
the petition OF Elizabeth Turner, mulatto girl
apprenticed under the Negro Apprentice law of

operation.

side of the petitioner, the respondent declining
to employ counsel, and leaving his case with
the Court.

declined to entertain petitions of habeas
corpus in similar cases. The above decision
will, If enforced, liberate every negro appren-

on the Platte river has fairly begun. Ranches

dered daily. General Smith and staff passed
Fort George yesterday en- route for Fort Phil.

text:
A Western correspondent of the Cincin-
natl Commercial tells the following story !:
The Indians had planted, weeded and care
fully tended upward of a thousand acres OF
corn. During the entire spring and sum-
mer-from the time the tiny seed had been
buried in the earth till it burst and shot
forth its green leaves-till the thousand
acres were green with waving tassels and
lefty spires-till the stocks were heavy with
golden fruit-till then the squaws watched
it and talked over it, dreaming in their own
savage way of the comfort and support it
was to be to them in the winter. Last
week the armies OF grasshoppers,
like pestilence, landed in the coun-
try, and flying over the river in
squads and legions, looking like vast
clouds of dust against the horizon, now
dark spot against the clear blue ether, now
visible few feet above the earth-a vast
buzzing, chirping, moving mass, bearing
death in their touch, and starvation, suffer-
ing and want in their wake-came upon
the carefully watched corn of the Yanko-
mites, in a single night it disappeared.
The tall, straight stalks were bowed down;
the leaves, eaten through, wilted and died;
the kernels, half-ripe, were sucked of their
strength, the whole field was DESTROYED.
Touching enough to move the heart OF the
most stoical was the sight on the morrow.
Up and down the burrows all over the field
ran the squaws and children wailing and
crying piteously. They ran to the stalks
and bent them over, examining them
mournfully; they tore away the husks and
looked upon the eaten kernels and naked
cots with a strange look of SAVAGE
despair. Starvation seemed written on all
their faces. as with sad and dismal walls
and howls they came out of the field and
looked upon their papooses, who in Sleep
ing innocence they had left, some hung in
blankets to the fences and trees, and others
playing on the green sward. ave must
die, we must starve-our children must die,
starve. starve, starve," so utterly helpless
did they seem-so savagely hopeless. The
men wrapped their blankets around them
selves, and when the squaws told them the
news they said nothing, did nothing to in
dictate that any great emotion was stirring
within them, but their countenances look
ed SO woe begone, so heart-rendingly sad,
that if we were introduced to a legion of
people doomed to be damned, they could
not looked more sad than these poor Yank-
tonites. -'.---

Old Tammsny Hall il rapidly disappearing

happy and appropriate time for some more
important reformations in the society than that
of mere change OF location. They might
have properly inaugurated their corner stone
ceremonies with a remuneration of their old
copperhead dogmas and general breaking up
Of all their plundering "rings." But the lengthy
address which they have issued to their friends,
who are invited to join them on the Fourth Of
July, shows that they are still joined to their
idols, and all sensible people will let them
alone. They reafirm their State rights doc
trines, are oblivious of the fact that there has
been rebellion and a war, and denounce the
Congress OF the United States, fresh from the
people, as "unforgiving, intolerant and selfish
political conspira;ors, who have usurped the
executive control Of the government" With
these sentiments as their corner stone" their
society will soon follow their old hall and be
swept from the face Of the earth as useless and
offensive rubbish.

Congress and tho State Of Parties South.


We publish to-day another OF those interest
ing letters from one of our special correspond
ents ON the state Of political parties and the
political situation and prospects down South.
The progress of events under President John.
sons policy, including the rise, decline and
collapse of the Southern johnson reconstruc-
ton party; the organization and rapid strides
Of the republican party South, with negso suf.
frage and it's other powerful machinery, means
and agencies, until this party holds the ten
rebel States within It's grasp; the absence Of
any Southern organized opposition to the party,
and the general indifference, dependency or
disgust Of the opposition elements down there,
are oil presented as facts which are well estab-
lished. That the general conclusions Of the
writer. therefore, ara we'll founded We saanot
doubt especially when our political informa-
tion from all other sources South runs in the
same channel. ttsHtsrM


With the republican party, therefore, iden-
titled with the restoration plan Of Congress, in
undisputed possession Of the South, through
the powerful agencies Of the War Department,
its military commanders and forces, the Freed
mems Bureau, the freedmen's schools and
universal negro suffrage, and with the ex-rebel
opposition elements broken up, demoralzed,
hopeless Of resistance and disguised with
negro equality and with superiority over the
disfranchised whites, but little remains for
Congress to do beyond securing the ground
thus gained. Hence we may expect an
explanatory reconstruction bin from this COM
ing July session, calculated to bring back into
Congress and our national politics the ten
excluded Southern States, as republican States
out and out, every one of them. In view of
this object it is supposed that, as the republi-
cans have gained their present footing South
and as they will still gain strength by delay, the
different measures required in Southern State
reorganization will be so timed as to exclude
Ill these outside States from the Presidential
election of 1868. This Will simplify the
national issue very much, or reduce it to new
organization of parties from breakup Of the
overgrown republican camp into two new par
,ics--the party of Chase and the national banks,
and the party Of Grant, the army and the
people. Upon this tremendous issue we expect
the ground will be broken by this July session
Of Congress.

correspondent with Gen. Hancock's Indian
expedition, writing from Fort Hooker,
April 2, says: A council was held at Fort
Dodge on the 24th ult between Maj. Dodge
and several chiefs of the Kiowas. The lat
ter professed much friendship for the
whites, and desired to be at peace with
them, but states that the Blackfeet, Sioux,
Cheyennes, Arapahoes and Camanches are
determined on war and will have it. They
spoke about several Northern tribes band
ing together tor war, making overtures to
Southern tribes to join them, and predict
ing the whites would have their hands full.
The indications all favor grand Indian
confederation and bloody war.

held here last night. One hundred men
joined the Seventh regiment, and consid-
cradle amount of money was subscribed.

JUNCTION CITY, Kansas, Oct. 31.-The peace
commission reached Fort Harker this morning
Two thousand Cheyennes arrived at Medicine
Lodge creek on Sunday, including six hundred
warriors. They approached in five bands,
formed in line of battle, and charged across the
creek, yelling and firing their pistols. The Com
missioners met them at the creek and shook
hands with the chiefs


On Monday treaty of peace was agreed upon
and a reservation granted them. The reserva-
tion is bounded east by the Arkansas river, south
and west by the Semerone, aud north by
Kansas, and contains about nine thousand
square miles. The Government gives them
$4,000 annually and suit of clothing for each
person in the tribe, and builds houses for an
agent, farmer, miller, physician, blacksmith, ETC.


The Indians agree to keep the peace and not
modest railroads.


Roman Nose and Medicine Arrow, two head
chiefs, were not present. A large quantity of
presents was given them, including arms and
ammunition. This concludes the treaties with
Southern Indians.


The Commissioners next visit North Platte
and Laramie.

Boston, Sept A.-The funeral services over
the remains of the late Sir Frederick Bruce, the
British Minister, who died so suddenly at the
fremont House last week took place in the
Trinity (Eplscopal) Church in this city this
forenoon. The attendance was very large, and
the exercises, consisting of the simple Episcopal
service, were very brief and impressive. As
mark of respect to the deceased the Office of the
British Consul was closed, flags on the city,
State, and general Government buildings were
dl played aC balt-mast, and the bells OF the city
churches were tolled during the progress of the
services.


Among those present to pay the last tribute
of respect TO the memory OF the deceased were
the n embers of the English Diplomatic Body OF
Washington, the British and other foreign con-
suls; the various officers of the United States
army from the forts, including Major General
Foster and General Benham; Commodore Rod
gers and all the other officers of the Charles
town Navy Yard ; Senator Wilson, General
Banks, and other Massachusetts members of
Congress; Governor Bullock and stat, Mayor
Norcross and members OF the City Government,
Collector Russell and other Custom House
officers, the Judges of the Supreme and Supe-
rior Courts, and various other high officials and
prominent citizens. There was also present
delegation OF about twenty of the Free Briton
Mutual Benefit Society of Montreal, and also
representatives of the Scots Charitable Society
and Briton Charitable Association of Boston.
The only procession was that inside the
church, when the remains were taken from the

The raw head and bloody bones of ferocious
Fenianism has again presented itself to the ex
cited imaginations of the Canadian people. In
the Convention which was held the other day
in Chicago to raise more funds on Fenian
bonds the Canadians could see nothing but
formidable organizations for the invasion of

meetings that have been held for the purpose
of letting off the efervescence that the recent
outbreak in Ireland erected among the Irish
in this country, have tended to throw our
neighbOrs over the border into a dreadful
state of bloodthirstiness. Regulars and
volunteers, with muskets and field pieces,
swords and sabres, have been pressed on to
the frontier, with the full expectation of meet
ing armed bands of Fenian invaders. We
are of opinion, however, that the Canadians
this time will find little cause for their prema-

SUsrIcIoUs.-Strange females, some of
them peddling cosmetics and other little
notions, visit the dwellings of citizens in
various localities daily, and their singular
movements are calculated to excite suspi-
cion. Wherever they find doors unlocked
they enter unceremoniously, without ring
ing the bells or otherwise making their
presence known, ard proceed to recon-
noitre the apartments. When detected,
they coelly apologize for the intrusion,
making inquiries for some person un-
known to the family, and gracefully re


tire. The other day one of these uncere-
monious visitors was found in the parlor
of a Market street residence, picking up
small rticles of value that were lying
around loose. and when confronted by the
lady of the house, told such plausible
story that she was permitted to depart.
Many other families have been annoyed by
the same kind of suspicious intruders
People should keep their front doors locked
during the day and evening, and the police
should look out for these strange females
who go about seeking opportunities to
pluader the dwellings of our citizens.
